name: Card sort
intent: Expose the taxonomy the human already holds by making them move pieces.
when: prioritising, clustering, or when the human is arguing with themselves
prompt: Move the pieces into piles. The argument you have while placing one is the useful part.
readback: The grouping is the insight. Ask which pile was hardest to place — that card names the tension.

claims.claim: Physically rearranging external objects to think, rather than to reach a physical goal, reduces the cognitive cost of a problem and improves or speeds its solution compared with manipulating the same elements mentally.
claims.construct: epistemic action; interactivity in problem solving

claims.claim: Having people sort items into their own groups reveals the categories and dimensions they actually use, including ones they cannot readily state.
Items placed inside the same bounded region are perceived as belonging together, even against other grouping cues, so labelled zones make category membership readable at a glance.
claims.construct: the Gestalt principle of common region (perceptual grouping)

grounding.helps: when the categories are real but unstated and placing each card forces a choice; sorting shows which categories a person uses, and moving physical pieces helped in a few small problem-solving studies
grounding.backfires: when printed column headings impose categories that are not the person's own, or the finished piles look tidier than the thinking behind them; neither risk has been tested
